Estación Palabra in Nuevo Laredo will host the Festival Tamaulipas Lee from Tuesday, Nov. 10, through Friday, Nov. 13, with book presentations, poetry readings and writing workshops for young people and the general public, according to CML Noticias.

The festival is organized by the Nuevo Laredo municipal government through its Directorate of Art and Culture, in coordination with the Government of the State of Tamaulipas and participating cultural institutions, with the goal of bringing reading and literary creation closer to the community.

The program opens Tuesday, Nov. 10, at 11 a.m. with the presentation of the book “Crónica de la aviación de Nuevo Laredo,” by author Raúl Llamas, in the Sala Literaria at Estación Palabra. The event is aimed mainly at young people interested in learning the history of aviation in the city, according to CML Noticias.

On Wednesday, Nov. 11, at 6 p.m., poet Marisol Vera Guerra will present the poetry recital “Afuera cantan las cicatrices de un árbol,” with Marcos Rodríguez Leija as presenter. The recital is open to the general public.

On Thursday, Nov. 12, from 4 to 8 p.m., writer Alfredo Marko will lead a crime-fiction workshop, where participants can learn tools and narrative techniques of the genre.

The festival closes Friday, Nov. 13, from 4 to 8 p.m., with the narrative workshop “Journaling para contar historias,” led by Dulce Gabriela Gutiérrez, focused on personal writing as a way to develop stories and express ideas.

People interested in the workshops can register through the sign-up links published by the organizers. The municipal government invited families, students and everyone interested in culture to take part in the four days of activities at Estación Palabra, according to CML Noticias.

Sources: CML Noticias; Desde Donde Estamos.
